subject: Request: Temporary latency tolerance for model v9.2 spike (decision needed 2026-05-18)
messages:
From: Tom Walters <tom.walters@bluebridge.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@bluebridge.ai
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected p95 jump after v9.2 rollout — need temporary SLA accommodation

Hi Irene / Kimberly,

Quick note from our ops team: after the v9.2 rollout yesterday we observed sustained p95 latency climb for our chat endpoint (model: v9.2-custom) from ~160ms to ~540ms during peak. This started around 23:10 UTC and has been intermittent since. Attached are a short sample of traces and a condensed latency CSV.

BlueBridge is on a 99.95% p95 SLA for live requests. We understand rollouts sometimes introduce regressions, but traffic is production and this is impacting user experience for a subset of customers. Can your team either:

- Temporarily allow a latency tolerance (SLA carve-out) for the next 48 hours while you investigate, OR
- Pin our traffic back to the v9.1 variant (we need a planned change window)

We need a decision by Monday 2026-05-18 17:00 PT so we can update our customer comms. Also copying Contracts in case any credits or formal exceptions are needed.

Thanks — Tom

--
Tom Walters
Head of Platform Ops, BlueBridge AI
ops@bluebridge.ai

Attachments:
- latency-samples-0516.json (6KB)
- redwood-trace-0516.zip (12MB)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Walters <tom.walters@bluebridge.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected p95 jump after v9.2 rollout — need temporary SLA accommodation

Tom — thanks for flagging and for the alert traces. We see the same signal in our monitoring. High level:

- Root cause hypothesis: a collector-path change in v9.2's KV cache coalescing that increases tail latency under specific tokenization patterns (seen in your traces).
- Impact window: intermittent during peak traffic; not a full outage but p95/99 elevated for ~10-20% of requests in a subset of tenants.

Immediate options (pros/cons):
1) Pin BlueBridge to v9.1 (safe, quick) — requires a controlled traffic shift (5–10 minutes) and rollback approval from product ops.
2) Staged traffic split (70% v9.1 / 30% v9.2) with automatic rollback if p95 > 300ms for 10m consecutive — keeps progressive testing but reduces exposure.
3) SLA carve-out (temporary tolerance) — administrative only, needs Sales/Contracts signoff; doesn’t change runtime.

Kimberly / Marcus / Monica: please advise on feasibility and required approvals. Tom: if you prefer a pin, let us know and we will schedule the traffic cut and a post-change verification.

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0148

--
Quoted original attachments preserved.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Walters <tom.walters@bluebridge.ai>, contracts@bluebridge.ai
Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected p95 jump after v9.2 rollout — need temporary SLA accommodation

Internal summary and recommendation:

- We can perform an immediate pin of BlueBridge traffic to v9.1. Ops will need a 15-minute change window and will run a validation job (synthetic + quick scan of KV hit/miss rates).
- Staged split is possible but requires us to hold off on the full rollback and adds monitoring overhead; it is preferable if BlueBridge wants progressive verification.
- SLA carve-out: Contracts signals that a short administrative "grace period" (48 hours) can be granted for documented incidents, but credits or formal SLA amendments take longer and need exec signoff.

Requesting approval: Irene, do you authorize the pin now (we can do it within the hour), or would you prefer staged split? If Irene approves, I'll open the change ticket and ping SRE.

Kimberly Park
Head of Enterprise Sales — West
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Tom Walters <tom.walters@bluebridge.ai>
Cc: contracts@bluebridge.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 16:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected p95 jump after v9.2 rollout — need temporary SLA accommodation

Decision and next steps: approved pin to v9.1 (emergency traffic re-route).

What we did:
- At 15:05 PT we cut BlueBridge to v9.1 (100%) and disabled the v9.2 variant for that tenant. Change window 15 minutes; verification completed at 15:25 PT.
- Observed p95 drop from ~520ms -> ~165ms in production samples within 8 minutes of the cut.
- Saved traces and post-change report attached (sla-terms-v2.pdf is the incident notes we will share with Contracts).

Follow-up items:
- Marcus / SRE to run a post mortem focused on KV coalescing heuristic in v9.2 (action owner: Marcus Lin).
- Monica to coordinate SLAs/credits comms with BlueBridge (action owner: Monica Patel).
- Kimberly to confirm whether BlueBridge requests a formal credit or just an incident report.

Tom — sorry for the disruption. We'll send the incident summary and timeline by EOD and schedule a technical review with your engineering team if you'd like.

Irene Choi
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

Attachments:
